reflection.baby_young: At {age_label}, this is a lovely age to start. In my words: it's more sleep shaping at this age than the sleep training element.
reflection.baby: At {age_label}, the day matters as much as the night. We always bang on about it: 75% of sleep training is the work in the day.
reflection.toddler: At {age_label}, it's about a routine they can count on and boundaries you can hold. My mantra is assisted days, independent nights.

reflection_struggle.night_wakes: {struggle_label} is one of the most common things parents tell me about, and there's usually more we can shift than it feels like at 3am.
reflection_struggle.short_naps: {struggle_label} are so often about timing, and timing is something we can work on together.
reflection_struggle.contact_naps: {struggle_label} can be shifted gently, at a pace you're comfortable with.
reflection_struggle.feed_to_sleep: {struggle_label} is a habit, not a problem you caused, and habits can change.
reflection_struggle.day_night_mixup: {struggle_label} is very normal early on, and the right day rhythm helps it settle.
reflection_struggle.overtired: {struggle_label} often eases with small changes to timing through the day.
reflection_struggle.no_routine: {struggle_label} is a great place to start, because we get to build it the right way from the beginning.
reflection_struggle.early_rising: {struggle_label} usually has a reason behind it, and we'll look at the whole day to find it.
reflection_struggle.nap_transition: {struggle_label} is a tricky patch, and getting the timing right makes it much smoother.
reflection_struggle.bedtime_battles: {struggle_label} are exhausting, and a predictable routine is where we start.
reflection_struggle.regression: {struggle_label} can knock everyone around. It's not because you've done anything wrong.
reflection_struggle.nap_refusal: {struggle_label} is so common at this age, and it's often about timing rather than your little one being difficult.
reflection_struggle.cot_to_bed: {struggle_label} goes more smoothly with a plan and a bit of patience.
reflection_struggle.cosleeping_transition: {struggle_label} works best gradually, at a pace that suits your family.

in_the_moment.body: The Snooze Specialists and I are in the forum Monday to Friday answering your sleep questions. You won't be guessing on your own.

body.baby_young: Start building a light, flexible routine.
body.baby: Start layering in consistent naps and bedtime.
body.toddler: Start reinforcing consistent boundaries at bedtime.

for_you.title: For you
for_you.sleep_tonight: You told me more sleep tonight matters most. Your start-here step is the one change I'd make first, so tonight has the best chance.
for_you.predictable_day: You told me a predictable day matters most. The day work comes first in Snooze, so you'll know what's coming and when.
for_you.confident_bedtime: You told me confidence at bedtime matters most. You'll know exactly what to do, and you can ask us when you're unsure.
for_you.feel_myself: You told me feeling like yourself again matters most. Better sleep for them is where that starts, and you're allowed to want this for you too.
for_you.partner_aligned: You told me being on the same page as your partner matters most. Your plan is easy to share, so you're both doing the same thing.

safety.title: A quick note first

note.feeding_weight: A feeding or weight worry is worth talking through with your GP, paediatrician or child health nurse: they're the right people for this one. A consult with me can help with the sleep side alongside that.
note.health: A health concern like reflux, breathing or illness is one to talk through with your GP, paediatrician or child health nurse first. A consult with me can help with the sleep side alongside that.
note.sleep_safety: Questions about safe sleep are worth talking through with your GP, paediatrician or child health nurse, who can look at your specific setup. A consult with me can help with the sleep side alongside that.
note.parent_struggling: Thank you for telling me. You are not alone in this. Please talk to your GP about how you're feeling, or call one of the lines below. That support matters as much as the sleep. A consult with me can help with the sleep side alongside it.

support_lines: If you or your baby are in danger, call 000 (Australia) or 911 (US)
